findings.claim: The diff adds CANCELLED -> RUNNING as an allowed transition, directly violating the stated invariant that a CANCELLED task must never transition to RUNNING.
findings.failure_scenario: Calling transition(task, TaskState.RUNNING) on a task whose task.state is TaskState.CANCELLED now succeeds instead of raising ValueError, letting a cancelled task resume execution as RUNNING.

findings.claim: The function's docstring still states that a CANCELLED task has no outgoing transitions and cancellation is terminal (citing INV-1), but the code now contradicts this by allowing CANCELLED -> RUNNING.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller reading the docstring for transition() will believe CANCELLED is terminal and rely on transition() raising for any CANCELLED->X call, but transition(task, TaskState.RUNNING) will silently succeed when task.state is CANCELLED, contradicting the documented behavior.
